paragraphs.text: MemVault — The Shared Memory Layer for Every AI Agent You Run. Self-hosted, open-source MCP memory s
erver with auto-injection, hybrid (BM25+vector) search, and zero-config sync — works with Codex, Cla
ude Code, Cursor, dsh, and any Agent client.
# MemVault
## How It Works
MemVault is a pipeline, not a single script. Every stage below is a shipping module:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
- **Storage:** SQLite with bundled FTS5 (full-text search); embeddings stored int8-quantized (~1/4 t

he size of f32 at near-identical ranking quality, legacy f32 rows still readable)
- **Retrieval:** B
M25 keyword search over FTS5 with CJK bigram tokenization (Chinese two-character words match correct
ly) and tiered match fallback (strict → relaxed unigram → synonym OR; relaxations are reported, neve
r silent), local-first embedding (in-process native by default — switch to local Ollama or any OpenA
I-compatible model), RRF fusion with per-result recall provenance (`kw#2`/`vec#5`), synonym expansio

n, relevance scoring, soft intent filtering
- **Pipeline:** Automatic entity extraction, delta-write
on save (near-duplicates skipped, similar memories absorb only the residual), semantic deduplicatio

n, time-based decay, archive of stale memories
- **Sync:** Zero-invasion file generation — `memvault
-cli sync` produces CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, etc. directly from database contents
## What MemVault Gives You
- **Auto-Injected Context:** Session start automatically pulls relevant memory by agent identity — M

UST-level rules land as instructions, not just chat history
- **Hybrid Retrieval:** BM25 + vector +
RRF fusion with synonym expansion, relevance scoring, and per-result provenance (which path recalled

each memory, at what rank) — available via CLI, MCP tool, and REST API
- **Explainable Injection:**
every candidate dropped on the way into an agent's context is recorded with a reason (budget, caps,

intent/type penalties) — "why didn't the agent get this memory?" always has an answer
- **Degrade B
efore Dropping:** when the token budget runs out, a memory is shortened — excerpt, then summary — ra
ther than cut, so more of the ranked list stays reachable at a lower per-memory cost. Shortened text
always carries a ` […]` marker and the level is reported separately from the dropped list, because
an abbreviation that *looks* complete is worse than a drop. MUST is never shortened: a binding rule

with its qualifying clause summarised away is worse than one that overflowed
- **MUST Enforcement:**
MUST-priority memories are never filtered or truncated. Always in context, always obeyed — trust co
mes from provenance (human-authored/reviewed), with an opt-in fallback for memories independently co
rroborated by multiple identity-verified agents (`MEMVAULT_CORROBORATION_GATE`), so a single spoofed

/compromised agent can't unilaterally inject a binding MUST
- **Multi-Agent Awareness:** Agent Regis

try with type/tag-based soft filtering (score demotion, not hard exclusion)
- **`agent_id` Is Proven
ance, Not a Filter:** retrieval never filters by `agent_id` — the field only records which agent wro
te a memory (`source_agent`). Every agent searches the same shared corpus; per-agent differences app

ly only at injection time (type/tag soft scoring via `agents.yaml` `inject_rules`)
- **MCP Proxy:**
Transparent proxy that injects memory into ANY upstream MCP server's responses — zero client changes
- **Compliance Tracking:** `inject_session_id` traces what was injected and measures follow-through

e Tracking:** `inject_session_id` traces what was injected and measures follow-through rate
[该节后续省略]
## Why MemVault

Storing and retrieving memories is solved — a dozen products do it well, and
since 2025 the Code Age

nts do it natively. What is *not* solved is the part after
retrieval: getting one shared corpus into

**every** agent you run, deciding
**what entitles a memory to bind** that agent, and knowing **whet

you run, deciding
**what entitles a memory to bind** that agent, and knowing **whether it obeyed**.

The claims below come from a 15-product survey refreshed 2026-11
(`docs/DESIGN.md` §2). They
are fal
sifiable — the table there names every product and every source.
### What only MemVault does
| Capability | What it actually means | Who else has it |
| **Follow-through tracking** | `inject_session_id` traces what was injected into which session and
measures whether the agent obeyed. Not "was it retrieved" — *was it followed* | **Nobody.** The clos
est is agent-memory's `audit`, which records who changed a memory, not whether an agent listened to

one |
| **Instruction-layer enforcement** | MUST memories are never filtered, never truncated, and a
re rendered as directives rather than context. A memory becomes a *constraint*, not a suggestion | *
*Nobody.** `MemoryTier.CORE` in agent-memory and core blocks in Letta mean "resident in context", wh

ich is not the same claim |
| **Trust-gated binding** | What entitles a memory to bind an agent: pro
venance, identity verification, and an opt-in corroboration gate so one spoofed or compromised agent
cannot unilaterally inject a MUST everyone obeys | **Nobody.** Multi-tenant ACLs answer *who may ac

cess*; this answers *what may be believed*. Different axis, and the survey has no column for it |
|
**Injection explainability** | Every candidate dropped on the way into an agent's context is recorde
d with a reason — budget, cap, intent penalty, review gate. "Why didn't the agent get this memory?"
always has an answer | agent-memory has retrieval *trajectory* (what was recalled). Nobody reports w

hat was **dropped and why** |
| **Review-gated agent edits** | An agent can propose a correction to
any memory, including a MUST — as a pending proposal that leaves the target live until a human decid

es | **Nobody.** Letta's agent self-edits memory directly, which is its own listed weakness |
| **Ta
sk-level evaluation** | `bench --judge` samples your own failure history and scores "plan without me
mory vs. plan with memory" against the known failure cause — task success, not retrieval recall | **
Nobody.** Every published number in this space is a recall metric |
### What MemVault does differently
| | Claude Code Auto Memory | Codex Memories | Mem0 | Zilliz memSearch | **MemVault** |
| Which agents see the memory | Claude Code only | Codex only | whatever embeds its SDK | per-tool p

lugins | **every agent you run, from one store** |
